_readme: Dog dermatology market — Poland. A TOP-DOWN ESTIMATE built entirely from free/public
sources. No public source measures this market directly, so every headline number here
is MODELLED, not observed. This file is the single reproducible source for the study page
dog-derm-poland.html — every figure on that page recomputes from the inputs below.
v2 (6 Aug 2026) adds: (a) a REFERENCE-MARKET panel — Germany, UK, Sweden, Czechia/Hungary —
used to transfer clinical RATES into Poland while anchoring MONEY locally; (b) TWO SCOPES,
v3 (6 Aug 2026) CORRECTS v2: Method 3 (Germany transfer) measures DERMATOLOGY DRUGS ONLY,
while Methods 1-2 measure DRUGS + SERVICES. v2 wrongly reported all three as converging on
one object and revised the band up on that basis. v3 separates the two objects, reverts the
drugs+services band to EUR 70-150M, and reports the drugs-only conflict as UNRESOLVED.

TRANSFER_RULE.principle: Rates transfer across markets; money does not.
TRANSFER_RULE.why: Clinical parameters are biological and broadly stable across comparable dog populations. Economic parameters scale with income, veterinary price level, and insurance penetration — all of which differ sharply between Poland and every reference market available.

scopes.PLAIN_STATEMENT: The scope is what dog owners in Poland pay to treat skin problems in their dogs, over one year.

vet_visits_plus_medicines.includes: Everything the owner pays when the dog is treated at a practice: the consultation, any tests, and the medicines prescribed.

medicines_only.includes: Just the medicines out of the line above. Nothing for the vet's time or tests.
medicines_only.measured_by: Method 3, and all published vendor figures

wider_market_report_definition.includes: All of the above, plus flea and tick products, shampoos and supplements bought in a shop or online without seeing a vet. Usually cats as well as dogs.

scopes.WARNING: Published market reports use the second or third row, not the first. A report headline compared against the first row will be wrong by two to four times.

fx.note: EUR/PLN ~4.30 (2024-25 band 4.2-4.4). USD/EUR ~1.08 (2024). Model is built in PLN; USD vendor figures converted at 1.08.

prevalence_ladder._warning: These four rows measure FOUR DIFFERENT OBJECTS and must never be mixed or averaged. The 74x spread between the first and second row is definitional, not geographic.

rows.note: One specific diagnosis, claims-based. A FLOOR for chronic atopic cases, not a skin-disease rate.
2nd most common disorder group. THE FIGURE USED IN THIS STUDY.
Partly overlapping with the skin group; not additive.

rows.source: Hill et al. 2006; Univ. Montreal small-animal clinic
rows.note: Share of VISITS, not share of dogs. Higher because affected dogs visit repeatedly.

reference_markets._role: Poland has no domestic prevalence or derm-market data. These four markets supply transferable rates and the scaling factors needed to move economics into Polish conditions.

poland.source: FEDIAF 2025 (2023 data); Eurostat comparative price levels 2024; pet-insurance penetration trade estimates

germany.role: PRIMARY TRANSFER SOURCE — the only reference market with a published country-level dermatology figure, which makes the backtest possible.
germany.source: Grand View Research Horizon (Germany veterinary dermatology drugs, 2024); FEDIAF; Eurostat
germany.CAVEAT: Vendor figure, unaudited. Global totals from competing vendors differ by ~2x (Grand View USD 17.4bn for 2024 vs Future Market Insights USD 9.7bn for 2025), so this anchor carries roughly +/-100% vendor uncertainty.

uk.role: PREVALENCE SOURCE — best clinical epidemiology available anywhere (VetCompass primary-care, large sample). Economics NOT transferred.

sweden.role: DEFINITIONAL CONTROL — near-universal insurance yields exceptional registry data, but its 0.17%/yr atopic-dermatitis incidence measures a narrow diagnosis, not skin disease broadly. Included to prove the prevalence ladder, not to set the rate.

czechia_hungary.role: ECONOMIC ANALOGUES — closest to Poland in income and vet-market structure. Used to confirm Poland's price level (72) sits in a coherent CEE band rather than being an outlier. Too data-thin to supply prevalence or market size.

scaling_factors._use: Applied ONLY to money transferred from a reference market into Poland. Never applied to clinical rates.

price_level_poland_vs_germany.basis: Eurostat comparative price levels: Poland 72 vs Germany ~110 on EU=100 → ratio ~0.65. Polish vet visit 100-250 PLN (EUR 23-58) vs German basic care EUR 100-250/yr corroborates.

treatment_seeking_poland_vs_germany.basis: Pet insurance penetration <10% (PL) vs ~20% (DE). Uninsured owners defer follow-ups and decline referrals, so fewer billed episodes per case — not merely cheaper ones.

dog_population.source: FEDIAF Facts & Figures 2025 (2023 pet population data)
dog_population.note: 4th largest dog population in the EU; highest per-capita dog ownership in Europe (~49% of households).

derm_episode_rate_per_year.source_proxy: UK VetCompass — skin disorders ~12.6% one-year period prevalence.
derm_episode_rate_per_year.PROXY_LIMITATION: No Polish national prevalence dataset exists. Rate is transferred from the UK under the TRANSFER_RULE above. Breed mix, climate and treatment-seeking behaviour could push the Polish rate off the UK one.

annual_derm_spend_per_treated_dog_pln.source: Polish price points ONLY (not transferred): consultation 100-250 PLN (PETHELP/Vivigo 2024-25); Apoquel 16mg ~46-90 PLN per 20-tablet pack (Allegro 2026); USG ~160 PLN. Simple episode ~150-400 PLN; chronic atopic case ~1,500-4,000 PLN/yr. Blend is dominated by simple cases.
annual_derm_spend_per_treated_dog_pln.note: Blended average, NOT a chronic-case cost.

method_2_top_down_envelope._calc: EUR {900,1400}M x companion{0.50,0.65} x dog{0.55,0.65} x derm-revenue{0.10,0.20}

method_3_germany_transfer._calc: EUR 1062M x (1-0.4523) ex-antiparasitic = EUR 582M; x dog-share{0.55,0.65} = EUR 320-378M; / 10.6M German dogs = EUR 30-36/dog; x scaling{0.45,0.65} = EUR 13.5-23.4/dog; x 8.1M Polish dogs
method_3_germany_transfer.note: Reports EUR 110-188M for drugs alone, which EXCEEDS the methods 1-2 estimate for drugs AND services. That is a genuine contradiction, not a convergence.
method_3_germany_transfer.measures: DRUGS ONLY — not comparable to methods 1 and 2

A1_drugs_and_services_eur_million.basis: Methods 1 and 2 only — the two routes that actually measure this object, both anchored on Polish price data.

A2_drugs_only_eur_million.basis: A1 x drug share of a derm episode (40-55%). Consult and diagnostics dominate simple cases; medication dominates chronic ones.

UNRESOLVED_CONFLICT.likelier_culprit: The vendor anchor. Competing publishers differ ~2x on the same global market, and Grand View's Germany figure would imply German owners spend EUR 30-36/dog/yr on clinical derm drugs alone. But the alternative reading - that the Polish vet-services envelope understates companion-animal spend - cannot be ruled out from public data.
UNRESOLVED_CONFLICT.how_to_settle_it: One Kynetec Poland data point, or any measured Polish derm drug sales figure, resolves this immediately. Until then the drugs-only number carries a 2-4x uncertainty and should be quoted as a range, not a point.

reconciled.REVISION_HISTORY: v1: EUR 70-150M (methods 1-2). v2: raised to EUR 90-160M on the mistaken basis that method 3 measured the same object. v3: reverted to EUR 70-150M for drugs+services; method 3 reclassified as a drugs-only upper-bound check.

scope_A_clinical.OBJECT_WARNING: Methods 1-2 measure DRUGS + SERVICES. Method 3 measures DRUGS ONLY. They are NOT three estimates of one quantity and must not be intersected or averaged.

germany_transfer._calc: EUR 1062M x dog-share{0.55,0.65} = EUR 584-690M; / 10.6M = EUR 55-65/dog; x scaling{0.45,0.65} = EUR 25-42/dog; x 8.1M Polish dogs

reported.note: The lower bound is HALVED from the transfer result to carry the ~2x disagreement between vendors on the global total. Scope B is therefore LESS certain than Scope A despite looking more official — its uncertainty is definitional and vendor-driven, not Poland-specific.

scope_ratio.note: Scope B / Scope A. Definition moves the answer more than prevalence and spend uncertainty combined.

veterinary_facilities.unit: licensed animal-treatment establishments (zaklady lecznicze dla zwierzat)
veterinary_facilities.source: Krajowa Izba Lekarsko-Weterynaryjna / WetSystems register; ~72% are clinics, avg ~1.5 vets each. Business-directory counts run higher (8,800 IBISWorld; ~12,700 CompanyData) because they include all registered vet businesses.
veterinary_facilities.note: Free, public, complete national register at wetsystems.org.pl — countable by voivodeship.

supply_side.regional_concentration: Mazovia (Warsaw) ~1,691 vet businesses, Greater Poland ~850, Silesia ~666, Lower Silesia ~612 (business-directory basis).

poland_vet_services_market.source: IBISWorld Veterinary Services in Poland (~EUR 1.4bn, 2026); Ken Research (~USD 0.9-1.5bn); Eurostat production value EUR 827.6M (2023) → ~EUR 997M by 2028.
poland_vet_services_market.note: Whole veterinary market — includes farm/livestock work, not companion-animal only.

derm_share_of_canine_clinical_spend.note: Dermatology is ~15-25% of consultation VOLUME but less of REVENUE — skin visits are cheaper than surgery or dentistry.

known_breaks_and_limits: EU veterinary prices rose ~37% since 2015 and are still running ~6%/yr vs ~2% general inflation — any figure older than ~2 years understates current spend.
The top-down envelope captures clinic-channel spend only, so it structurally leans low.
Vendor country figures are unaudited and mutually inconsistent by ~2x at the global level.
No deflator applied: all figures are a single recent year (2023-2026), not a time series.
Sweden's 0.17%/yr is atopic-dermatitis incidence from insured claims — NOT comparable to the UK's 12.58% all-skin period prevalence.

sources.what: Prevalence of commonly diagnosed disorders in UK dogs under primary veterinary care
Prevalence, diagnosis and treatment of dermatological conditions in small animals in general practice
Incidence of and risk factors for atopic dermatitis in insured Swedish dogs
Cost of a Polish vet visit, 2024-2025 price survey

paid_vendors.gives: Actual pharmaceutical sales through the vet channel and patient visits/spend by therapeutic area, monthly, by country — the only real measured source for Polish derm sales.
Country-level veterinary dermatology drug outlook (Poland cut available).
Polish pet ownership, spend and channels; weak on pharma specifics.
